questions.note: Height, head size and limb lengths sit close to the reference in the onion, legs longer as declared. Upper arms read as thick smooth tubes and the gloved hands look oversized; shoulders slightly narrow where the reference's pauldrons widen them. Proportions are the strongest part of the build.

Stance, lean, elbow positions and the carbine diagonal follow the reference in the onion. The outline is softer and narrower at the shoulders and chest because the pauldrons and carrier lack bulk, and the thighs are pencil-thin where the reference's are baggy; the lower legs flare instead.

Gaiter, carrier with three front pouches, antenna on the left back, pauldrons, forearm guards, gloves, belt, thigh rigs, knee pads and boots are all present and roughly where drawn. Pauldrons are flat cards rather than shaped shells, the chest pouches are small boxes, and a back pouch stands off the hip.

No obvious clipping in these views, but layering is weak: trousers cling like leggings over crotch and seat, pauldrons and the carrier's shoulder pads stand off as thin cards, a pouch behind the right hip floats clear of the body, and elbow pads are edge-on slivers rather than pads over the sleeve.

The man and his kit read light and clean: a thin flat carrier with none of the reference's layered webbing, thin band-like arm armour, skin-tight thighs, smooth tube sleeves. The reference's bulk and clutter are missing, so he reads younger and lighter than the drawn soldier.

Support hand closes over the handguard plausibly and the carbine line matches. The firing hand lies on the receiver with a stiff straight index and its fingers do not visibly wrap the pistol grip; both gloves are posed like mannequin hands, so the hold reads placed rather than gripped.

defects.what: Hair is a smooth dark shell with a hard cut-out hairline and jagged triangular shards on the crown; no strands, no fade at the temples, it reads as a rubber cap.
defects.fix: A short crew cut: strand cards or curves, density fading to stubble at temples and nape, a soft broken hairline.

defects.what: The soldier's right pauldron is a paper-thin flat card tilted off the deltoid with a gap beneath, no thickness and no curvature following the shoulder.
defects.fix: A molded shell several mm thick that wraps the deltoid and is strapped down onto the sleeve.

defects.what: The white speckle wear on pauldron, arm bands and forearm guards is one high-contrast noise at one scale everywhere, reading as procedural salt rather than wear.
defects.fix: Wear concentrated on edges and raised corners, low contrast, scuffed through to substrate, with dirt in recesses and flat areas left mostly intact.

defects.what: The carrier front is a flat khaki slab with dead-straight edges and soft rounded corners; the mag pouches are plain boxes; no PALS, binding, stitching or fabric creasing.
defects.fix: JPC-class front: MOLLE rows or laser-cut slots, bound edges, stitched pouches with flaps and bungee, fabric slack and creases.

defects.what: Trousers are skin-tight over crotch, thighs and seat (anatomical bulge in front, buttock seam at the back), then baggy below the knee; they read as leggings.
defects.fix: G3-class trousers hang from the hips with a crotch gusset, pocket volume and folds at the hip crease, loose over the thigh.

defects.what: Above both boots the trousers stack in regular horizontal rings like an accordion, the same on both legs.
defects.fix: Real stacking over a boot top is irregular, with diagonal folds and one or two deep breaks, best from a cloth simulation.

defects.what: The trouser fabric shows a coarse burlap weave far too large for ripstop, visible even in the full view, under soft cloud-noise camo with no defined edges.
defects.fix: A fine ripstop grid near invisible at this distance; camo and dirt with defined shapes, dirt heavier at knees and cuffs.

defects.what: The soldier's right boot vamp is a seamless smooth shell with one sweep line, no toe cap and no lacing toward the toe; it reads as a galosh or sneaker.
defects.fix: Zephyr class: suede and textile panels with seams, a rubber toe bumper, eyelets running down to the forefoot, creases at the flex point.

defects.what: Gloves are smooth rubber with sausage fingers, no knuckle guards, seams or palm patches, posed stiffly like mannequin hands.
defects.fix: M-Pact class: TPR knuckle and finger guards, stitched panels, synthetic leather palm, creasing at every knuckle.

defects.what: A tall pouch on the back of the belt stands away from the hip at an angle with a clear gap, not resting on the body.
defects.fix: It hangs from the belt and lies against the seat, following its curve.

defects.what: The top of the handguard renders as black-and-white zebra stripes, like hazard tape, from the rail slots or an aliased texture.
defects.fix: Rail teeth read as dark anodised ridges with small soft highlights, never high-contrast bands.

defects.what: The elbow pad seen edge-on is a paper-thin bright metal disc standing off the elbow; the soldier's right elbow shows the same sliver.
defects.fix: An elbow pad is a padded shell about 15 mm thick wrapping the joint, matte, strapped over the sleeve.

defects.what: The sleeve is a seamless smooth tube with no folds at the elbow bend, no seams and no fabric texture; the shirt reads as a wetsuit.
defects.fix: Combat shirt sleeves bunch and crease at the elbow inside, show seams and a matte knit texture.

defects.what: Small stray triangular spikes poke up from the top of the soldier's right shoulder, like torn cloth or stray hair geometry.
defects.fix: Remove the stray faces; the shoulder line is a clean fabric curve under the carrier strap.

defects.what: Knee pads are pillowy rounded boxes with even leopard-spot tan blotches that read as a camo decal, not scuffing; no hard cap edge.
defects.fix: AirFlex class: a hard faceted cap with a defined rim over a fabric sleeve, scuffs on the most prominent face and dust in creases.

defects.what: The carrier's shoulder pad is a thin flat card with stepped edges and a black void beneath it.
defects.fix: A padded shoulder strap with thickness and bound edges, resting on the shoulder.

ranked: [D1] The hair is a dark rubber cap with a cut-out hairline and shards on the crown; with the declared default skin, the head reads as a game NPC at a glance.
[D5] Trousers are skin-tight from waist to knee, showing crotch and buttocks like leggings, then baggy below; real G3-class trousers hang loose from the hips.
[D3] Every hard plate carries the same uniform white speckle; it reads as procedural salt noise. Real wear sits on edges and corners, low contrast, with dirt in the recesses.
[D4] The carrier front is a flat khaki slab with dead-straight edges and box pouches, no PALS, binding or stitching; the reference carrier is busy, bulky webbing.
Mass overall: thin carrier, thin band-like arm armour, slim thighs and smooth sleeves make the man read lighter, younger and cleaner than the reference's loaded soldier.
[D2] Pauldrons are paper-thin flat cards tilted off the deltoids, with no molded curvature or thickness.
[D13] Sleeves and shirt are seamless smooth tubes with no folds at elbow or shoulder and no fabric texture; it reads as a wetsuit.
[D9] Gloves are smooth rubber with sausage fingers and mannequin poses; no knuckle guards, seams or palm patches.
[D8] The soldier's right boot is a smooth seamless shell with no toe cap or forefoot lacing; it reads as a galosh, not a Zephyr-class boot.
[D7] The trouser weave is coarse burlap at a far too large scale, visible in the full view, under soft cloud-noise camo.
[D6] Trouser hems stack in regular accordion rings, identical on both legs, instead of irregular blousing over the boots.
[D15] Knee pads are pillowy boxes with leopard-spot decal blotches, missing the hard faceted cap and rim.
[D10] A pouch on the back of the belt stands off the hip with a visible gap, floating rather than hanging against the seat.
The carbine is uniform matte grey with no anodising variation, edge wear or dust; next to the worn kit it reads as an untextured asset.
The firing hand lies on the receiver with a stiff straight index and no visible wrap around the pistol grip, so the hold reads placed, not gripped.
[D11] The handguard top renders as black-and-white zebra stripes like hazard tape.
[D12] Elbow pads seen edge-on are thin bright metal slivers standing off the elbows.
[D16] The carrier's shoulder pads are thin flat cards with stepped edges and a black void beneath.
[D14] Stray triangular spikes poke up from the top of the soldier's right shoulder.
